+## What
+
+Task `^1fjmy9f`'s new real-model integration test (`PromptCacheHybridReuseTests.swift`) proved that hybrid Mamba/attention prompt-cache reuse (task `^r9rf5g7`) never actually engages against a real `mlx-community/Qwen3.6-27B-mxfp4` session: `supportsPromptCacheReuse == true`, but round 2's `cachedTokenCount` is `0` when it should be `>= 26`. This is NOT the narrow "EOS-terminated round" case the original design doc anticipated — round 1 in the real test hit `maximumResponseTokens` (a budget cutoff), not natural EOS, and STILL triggered the drop. The user has directed: fix this for real, do not document/scope it away.
+
+## Root cause (partially traced by reading `Libraries/MLXLMCommon/Evaluate.swift`'s `TokenIterator`, needs verification against the ACTUAL code path `respond()` uses)
+
+`TokenIterator.next()` uses a "return previous, prefetch next" pipelining design (`Evaluate.swift` ~line 744-759): each call captures `previousY`, calls `step(previous: previousY)` (which FEEDS `previousY` through the model, physically advancing `cache.offset`/Mamba state by exactly 1), then returns `previousY`. In the normal per-call case this is exactly 1:1 (fed token == returned token, no drift).
+
+The drift traced so far, specifically for the **EOS-terminated case** (`generateLoopTask` in the same file, ~line 1871-1899): when `iterator.next()` returns a stop/EOS token, `step()` has ALREADY fed that EOS token through the model (advancing the cache) BEFORE the stop-check runs — but the outer loop's own `tokenCount` (which feeds `generatedTokenIDs`) is only incremented in the non-stop branch, so it never counts the EOS token. Net effect: `cache.offset` ends up exactly 1 token ahead of `generatedTokenIDs.count`. Crucially, this extra token's IDENTITY IS fully known — it's the literal `token` value the stop-check already has in hand (the real EOS/stop token id) — it is simply excluded from `generatedTokenIDs` by design (EOS isn't real emitted content).
+
+**NOT YET VERIFIED**: the real test's round 1 was NOT EOS-terminated (hit `maximumResponseTokens` instead), yet still showed the same one-ahead drift. This means either (a) the maxTokens cutoff path has an analogous "fed but not counted" step somewhere in whichever ACTUAL code path `respond()` uses for this model (likely `Executor.runReasoning` or `runToolCallReasoningPhase` in `Libraries/MLXFoundationModels/MLXLanguageModel.swift`, NOT the generic `generateLoopTask` traced above — these are reasoning-aware paths with their OWN token loop, not necessarily identical in structure), or (b) there's a different mechanism entirely. **This must be read and confirmed directly in the actual executed path before any fix is designed** — do not assume the `generateLoopTask`/EOS mechanism generalizes without checking.
+
+## Why "just trim" or "just store anyway" are NOT valid fixes
+
+- Hybrid stacks can't trim (`MambaCache`/`ArraysCache.isTrimmable == false`) because Mamba's recurrent state is a collapsed running summary with no per-position history — there's no way to "undo" the last fed token's contribution by truncation, unlike attention's append-only, position-addressable K/V.
+- Storing the checkpoint anyway, keyed on the SHORTER observed-token sequence while the actual `cache`'s physical state (both KVCacheSimple `.offset` AND Mamba's recurrent state) reflects ONE MORE token than that key claims, would be unsound: restoring that checkpoint later and feeding the real next suffix would silently misalign RoPE position offsets by one and attend to a phantom extra position for attention layers, and feed Mamba a state that's already absorbed a token that isn't part of the claimed prefix. This is a correctness bug, worse than not caching at all — do not implement this.
+
+## Required fix (once the real path's exact mechanism is confirmed)
+
+The sound approach is very likely: **recover the true identity of the extra fed-but-uncounted token**, and store the hybrid checkpoint keyed on the FULL, TRUE token sequence (`slot.promptTokens + generatedTokenIDs + [theExtraToken]`) rather than trying to force the physical cache down to a shorter length it cannot actually represent. For the EOS case this is straightforward (the extra token IS the known stop-token id already in hand at the call site). For the maxTokens case, first determine (by reading the real path) whether an analogous "known extra token" exists there too, or whether the mechanism is different and needs a different sound recovery strategy.
+
+Do NOT weaken this to `cachedTokenCount > 0`, do not mark hybrid models as permanently unsupported for caching (already rejected once in `^r9rf5g7`'s history — do not repeat that mistake), and do not silently drop this task's rigor to make a test pass.
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+
+- [ ] Read and document the EXACT generation loop `respond()` uses for a reasoning-capable model like Qwen3.6 (likely `Executor.runReasoning`/`runToolCallReasoningPhase` in `MLXLanguageModel.swift`) and confirm precisely where/why a maxTokens-terminated round still ends up with `cache`'s true offset one ahead of `generatedTokenIDs.count`.
+- [ ] Implement a sound fix that lets hybrid checkpoints actually get stored on realistic rounds (both EOS-terminated and maxTokens-terminated), without corrupting the checkpoint's claimed token sequence vs. the cache's true physical state.
+- [ ] `IntegrationTesting/IntegrationTestingTests/MLXFoundationModelsIntegration/TextGeneration/PromptCacheHybridReuseTests.swift` (from `^1fjmy9f`) passes against the REAL `mlx-community/Qwen3.6-27B-mxfp4` model — run it for real, do not just reason about it.
+- [ ] No regression: `xcodebuild ... -only-testing:IntegrationTestingTests/PromptCacheReuseTests` (pure-attention path) still passes; `swift test` (full, unfiltered) stays green at whatever the current baseline is.
+- [ ] `PromptCache.cacheAdvanceOffset`'s doc comment (and any other doc comment describing the old "KNOWN, ACCEPTABLE DEGRADATION") is rewritten to reflect the actual fixed behavior, not left describing a degradation that no longer exists.
+
+## Scope
+
+Primarily `Libraries/MLXFoundationModels/MLXLanguageModel.swift` and `Libraries/MLXFoundationModels/PromptCache.swift`/`PromptCacheChunks.swift`. May require touching `Libraries/MLXLMCommon/Evaluate.swift` if the root mechanism genuinely lives there (e.g. exposing the pending/lookahead token's identity, or the maxTokens-path's equivalent) — that is in scope if the investigation shows it's required, since the user has explicitly asked for a real fix over a scoped-down one. Do not restructure unrelated parts of the generation loop beyond what's needed to expose/fix this specific mechanism.
